platform_notes: Our sheets put the Z line (Z6 PIN pad, Z8, Z9, Z11) on Dejavoo's Linux terminals running the Aura payment application, and the QD line (QD1 to QD5) on Android running the same Aura application, which Dejavoo's own guides call DvPay (AURA) and which sits beside a Market or DVStore app; files and parameters come down by TPN from Dejavoo's STEAM / iPOSpays systems. Dejavoo's quick reference guides are published per line (non-touch Z8, touch Z9/Z11, QD Terminal Line) and per program (EMV, Dual Pricing, True Cash Discount, each for retail and restaurant), and the menu steps differ between those programs. Dejavoo's all-models manual (V525.15) predates Aura, and the processor guides (PaymentCloud, Stax, Xplor Pay, PayCompass) describe their own builds, so their steps are kept separate from the maker's.

entries.title: Comm Error: check the connection icon in the status bar
steps: Check the status bar at the top of the terminal screen.
Look for the Wi-Fi symbol (three curved lines coming out of one dot) or the Ethernet symbol (three dots between outward-facing arrows).
Connect with the type your model supports: Stax lists Wi-Fi for the QD2, and Wi-Fi or Ethernet for the QD4.
A Comm Error is often, but not always, resolved by checking connectivity.
entries.quote: A Comm Error is often – but not always – resolved by checking connectivity issues.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Comm Error: run the terminal's network self-check
steps: Go to the home screen.
Select Settings.
Select Self-Check.
Select Network.
Select WiFi Network or Ethernet Network, whichever you want to check.
The check ends in either success or failure.
entries.quote: Select either WiFi Network or Ethernet Network, depending on which you want to check.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Comm Error: run a ping test from the terminal
steps: Go to the home screen and select Settings.
Select Self-Check, then Network, then WIFI Network, then Test WIFI.
Write down the IP Address and the public IP Address if there is one.
Go back twice with the left arrow at the bottom of the terminal.
Select Advance, then PingTool.
Enter the IP address and select Ping.
A few lines of data in the Ping Result means the test passed.
The word timeout in the Ping Result means the test failed.
entries.quote: If the Ping Result shows the word timeout, the Ping Test was unsuccessful.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Wi-Fi works but Ethernet does not (QD4)
steps: Make sure the Ethernet cords are plugged in properly and securely.
Plug one end into an Ethernet port on the wall, router or switch.
Plug the other end into the terminal's Ethernet port.
Check that the port is glowing green.
Try a different Ethernet cord.
If the port is not glowing green, the port has a problem and the terminal needs replacing.
entries.quote: Confirm the port is glowing green; if not, the port has an issue, and you'll need to replace the terminal.

entries.title: Terminal keeps turning off and on (reboot loop)
steps: Leave the terminal plugged in to a wall outlet, not a computer, for a few hours, preferably overnight.
The cause given: a nearly empty battery has enough power to turn on but not enough to stay on, so the terminal loops.
If it still has battery trouble after charging overnight, contact support because a replacement may be needed.
entries.quote: If the terminal keeps turning off and on, leave it plugged in for a few hours (preferably overnight) to an outlet, not to a computer.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: What the red charging light means
steps: A flashing red light means damage to the charging port.
A solid red light while plugged in means the terminal is charging.
entries.quote: Flashing = damage to charging port
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Red light is flashing
steps: A flashing red light means damage to the charging port.
Contact support: Stax lists a battery that is not charging among the hardware issues that go to Dejavoo Support.
entries.quote: Flashing = damage to charging port
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: QD2 shows a solid red light, is plugged in, but will not power on
steps: The battery may not be charging.
Remove the terminal's back cover to find the battery, which has a wire plugged into the terminal.
Carefully unplug the battery from the terminal, then firmly plug it back in.
Let it charge for 30 minutes.
Try turning the terminal back on.
entries.quote: Carefully unplug the battery from the terminal, and then firmly plug it back in.

entries.title: Troubleshooting step 1: check the time zone, date and time
steps: Go to the home screen and select Settings.
Select Date & Time.
Turn off Automatic time zone and pick the time zone by hand (Stax lists PST = GMT -07:00, MST = GMT -06:00, CST = GMT -05:00, EST = GMT -04:00).
Turn off Automatic date & time and set the date and time by hand.
Turn both Automatic time zone and Automatic date & time back on.
Turn on Use 24-hour format.
entries.quote: Toggle on both Automatic time zone and Automatic date & time.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Terminal keeps freezing or shows a spinning wheel
steps: It may have too many apps running at once.
Press and hold the home button (the circle at the bottom middle of the terminal) to see all open apps.
Swipe left on each window to close the app.
entries.quote: Then swipe left on each window to close the app.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Update the Market and DvPay (Aura) apps on a black QD terminal
steps: Go to the terminal's home screen and select Market.
Market should start updating by itself. If it does not, select Install or Update if shown. If it only says Open, it is already on the latest version.
Check DvPay next. If there is an Update or Install button, select it and let it run.
Batch out.
The batch should prompt an automatic download. If it does not, or no batch is open, a full download is needed.
entries.quote: On the next screen, Market should start automatically updating. If it does not, select Install or Update, if available. If it just says Open, it is on the latest version.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Update the DVStore and DvPay (Aura) apps on a white QD terminal
steps: Go to the terminal's home screen and select DVStore.
Select the menu (three lines) in the top left.
Select Update DVStore.
If the update fails, make sure the date and time are correct.
DvPay (Aura) updates automatically when DVStore updates.
Batch out. The batch should prompt an automatic download; if not, a full download is needed.
entries.quote: If the update fails, make sure the date/time is correct.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Perform a download to update the terminal
steps: Make sure the batch is closed.
Select the Aura app, then the Menu icon (3 horizontal lines).
Select Utility. If asked for a password, Stax gives 1234.
Select Software Download, then Connect, then Connection Type: Network.
Select Full download. If it says "No updates required", try again with Partial download.
Confirm the TPN that appears with the green key.
At Apply Updates? select Yes.
entries.quote: Select Full download. If a message appears that states "No updates required", reattempt and select Partial download.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

Contact support to have it resolved.
entries.quote: Bad BIN / Host Disconnect

entries.quote: Not connected to the SPIn Proxy server.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

steps: Stax lists updating the batch time as something that needs support to do.
entries.quote: This section details issues that require Partner Support to resolve.

entries.title: Hardware problems that go to Dejavoo Support
steps: These go to Dejavoo Support at 877-358-6797, ext. 2: battery not charging; factory reset; terminal not powering on even after charging; terminal not accepting a tapped transaction; terminal missing applications such as DvPay or DvStore/Market.
Dejavoo will advise and refer you back to your processor if a new terminal is needed.
entries.quote: If experiencing any of these hardware-specific issues, please contact Dejavoo Support directly at 877-358-6797, ext. 2.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Terminal will not accept a tapped (contactless) transaction
steps: Stax treats this as a hardware-specific issue.
Contact Dejavoo Support at 877-358-6797, ext. 2.
entries.quote: Terminal not accepting a tapped transaction.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: DvPay or DvStore/Market app is missing from the terminal
steps: Stax treats this as an issue for Dejavoo Support.
Contact Dejavoo Support at 877-358-6797, ext. 2.
entries.quote: Terminal missing applications such as DvPay or DvStore/Market.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Terminal will not power on even after charging
steps: Stax treats this as a hardware-specific issue.
Contact Dejavoo Support at 877-358-6797, ext. 2. They will say whether a new terminal is needed.
entries.quote: Terminal not powering on even after charging.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Register busy error (terminal integrated with a POS)
steps: The terminal is not on the "POS Online" screen, so the POS software cannot talk to it.
It can also mean the terminal is still processing a previous request.
entries.quote: The merchant is not on the "POS Online" screen, so Stax Pay is unable to communicate with the terminal.
entries.note: Stax's wording refers to its own Stax Pay software.

entries.title: Manually batch out
steps: On the terminal main page, select the Aura app.
Select the menu (3 horizontal lines).
Select Settlement.
Select Settle Daily Batch.
entries.quote: On the terminal main page, select the Aura app.

entries.title: Generate a custom report with Report Generator
steps: Open the DvPay (Aura) app.
Select Favourites (the star at the bottom centre of the screen), then Report.
Select Report Generator.
Choose the report type: Daily, Summary, Detailed Report or History Report.
Choose the payment type: All, Credit, Debit or EBT.
Choose the transaction type: All, Sale, Return, Void, Authorization, Ticket or Cash Advance.
Choose what to sort by: EDC, Transaction #, Transaction Type or Card Type.
Answer Yes or No when asked Save as Custom Report?
The report prints.
entries.quote: For the most customizable options, select Report Generator.

entries.title: Thermal paper size for the QD terminal
steps: Stax gives the paper dimensions as 2 1/4" x 50'.
Search for thermal paper in that size at your preferred retailer.
entries.quote: Order thermal paper Dimensions: 2 1/4" x 50'

entries.title: Change the sleep-mode setting
steps: Go to the home screen and select Settings.
Tap the Menu icon (3 horizontal lines) at the top right.
Select Display, then Sleep.
Set it to your preference.
entries.quote: Click on the Menu icon on the top right of the screen (3 horizontal lines).

entries.title: Change the screen font size
steps: Go to the home screen and select Settings.
Select the Menu (3 horizontal lines).
Select Display, then Font Size.
Change it to the size you want.
entries.quote: Modify to the desired size.

entries.title: Turn silent mode on or off
steps: Press and hold the power button on the left-hand side of the terminal.
Select Silent mode.
entries.quote: Press and hold the power button on the left-hand side of the terminal.

entries.title: What is in the QD4 box
steps: Check the box contains: the QD4 terminal, a power adapter, a USB power cable, a connector box (used for Ethernet) and a connector box adaptor.
entries.quote: Connector box (used for ethernet purposes)

entries.title: Power on the terminal for the first time
steps: Connect the USB power cable to the power adaptor and plug it into an outlet.
On a QD2, plug the other end into the terminal.
Press and hold the power button on the left-hand side of the terminal.
Wait for the home screen.
entries.quote: Press and hold the power button on the left-hand side of the terminal to power on.

entries.title: Connect to Wi-Fi
steps: From the home screen, tap the Settings icon in the top left-hand corner.
Select WLAN.
Tap your Wi-Fi network name.
If asked, enter the Wi-Fi password and press Connect.
The network should show CONNECTED.
If the terminal is integrated with another device, both must be on the same Wi-Fi network.
entries.quote: Your network should now show CONNECTED once completed.
entries.note: Stax's tutorial is written around the QD4 and QD2.

entries.title: Connect to Ethernet with the base port
steps: Connect the provided base port to the QD terminal.
Connect the Ethernet cable to the base port.
Connect the other end of the Ethernet cord to your router or wired Ethernet outlet.
entries.quote: Connect the opposite end of the ethernet cord to your router or wired ethernet outlet.

entries.title: Load receipt paper
steps: Paper loads at the top of the device.
Find the indents on the side of the machine and open the door.
Put the roll in with the top portion facing up.
Close the door with some paper hanging out.
entries.quote: Locate the indents on the side of the machine and open the door/flap to insert the paper roll.

entries.title: Receipts come out blank: test the paper and flip the roll
steps: On the home screen, select the Settings icon.
Tap the Self-Check icon.
Tap the Printer icon.
If the paper is in correctly the receipt prints with ink.
If it prints blank, flip the roll around and test again.
entries.quote: If entered properly, the receipt will print with ink. If the paper prints blank, flip the roll around and test again.

entries.title: Set the date, time and time zone
steps: On the home screen, select the Settings icon.
Select the three horizontal bars in the top right-hand corner.
Select Date and Time.
Recommended: keep automatic date, time and time zone turned on.
To set it by hand, turn off automatic date and time and automatic time zone, then use Set Date, Set Time and Time Zone.
entries.quote: For automatic date and time updates, ensure automatic date, time, and time zones are turned on by clicking the toggle button on the bottom to the right.

entries.title: Run a sale from the Aura app
steps: Open the Aura app on the terminal's home screen.
Tap the screen and select Credit or Debit.
Select Sale.
Enter the sale amount.
Insert, swipe or tap the card.
If it goes through, the device says Approved and the receipt prints.
entries.quote: If successful, the device will say Approved and the receipt will be printed.

entries.title: Void a transaction from Favorites
steps: Open the Aura app.
Tap the three horizontal lines symbol.
Select Favorites, then Void Transaction.
Choose Last Transaction, By Transaction # (the number is on the original receipt) or View All.
If asked, enter the manager password (default 1234) and press OK.
Confirm the transaction is the right one and select OK.
The terminal flashes an approval and prints a receipt.
entries.quote: By Transaction # - will void a specific transaction number (found on the original receipt)

entries.title: Refund a card
steps: Open the Aura app.
Tap Credit or Debit, then Return.
Enter the refund amount and press OK.
Tap, insert or swipe the card, or enter the full card number by selecting the three horizontal bars icon.
The terminal flashes an approval and prints a receipt.
Refunds typically process within 3-5 business days depending on the customer's bank.
entries.quote: Important: Refunds typically process within 3-5 business days depending on the customer's bank.

entries.title: Report types on the terminal and where to find them
steps: Open the Aura app and tap the three horizontal bars icon.
If asked, enter the manager password (default 1234) and press OK.
Select Applications, then Credit/Debit/EBT, then Reports.
Daily Report: a brief overview of the day's transactions.
Summary Report: a high-level summary plus summaries by transaction type.
Detailed Report: core details of every transaction, including last four card digits and times.
History Report: a summary of a specific day's transactions.
Report Generator: build custom reports. Custom Reports: reports you saved before.
entries.quote: Detailed Report - includes core details from every transaction, including last four card numbers and transaction times

entries.title: Connect to Wi-Fi on a non-touch Z terminal
steps: From the main screen, select F1.
Select Comm Status.
Select Wi-fi.
Enter the Wi-Fi password when asked. Press 0 on the keypad for special characters if needed.
Press the green button to connect.
The IP address should show with no zero, and it will show connected.
entries.quote: Enter Wi-Fi password when prompted (Hit 0 on the keypad for special characters if needed)

entries.title: Connect to Wi-Fi on a touch-screen model
steps: From the home screen, tap the Settings icon in the top left-hand corner.
Select WLAN.
Select Scan Network.
Tap your Wi-Fi network name.
Select Configure.
If asked, enter the Wi-Fi password and press Connect.
If the terminal is integrated with another device, both must be on the same Wi-Fi network.
entries.quote: Touch Screen Models (Z9, Z11 and QD line):

entries.title: Turn on the 3G (cellular) connection on a Z9
steps: Tap the three-line icon on the main screen to open the Services menu.
Tap Core.
Tap Utility and enter the manager password (1234 is the default).
Tap Communications, then Local Parms, then 3G/GPRS.
Tap Status, then Reconnect. The terminal shows GPRS Connecting.
Once connected, a 3G icon shows at the top of the main screen. Tap it for connection details.
Tap Ping and press 2 for Ping Google.
If it shows Ping Success, run a test sale.
entries.quote: Once connected, the main screen will display the 3G icon at the top of the screen.

entries.title: Connect a non-touch Z terminal to Ethernet and test it
steps: Unplug the machine.
Connect one end of the Ethernet cable to the LAN port on the back and the other to your modem or router.
Power the machine on.
From the main credit/sale screen press F1, then Comm Status, then Ethernet. If it shows LAN Active, look for your network IP address.
Press F1, Comm Status, then the down arrow twice for Ping.
Press 2 on the keypad for Ping Google.
Ping Success means you are ready to process. Run a test sale.
Ping Fails means check your network: reset your router and try again, or contact support.
entries.quote: If the terminal displays Ping Fails, check your network configurations. We usually recommend resetting your router and trying again. Or contact Stax support for additional assistance

entries.title: Terminal shows Ping Fails
steps: Check your network configuration.
Reset your router and try the ping again.
If it still fails, contact support.
entries.quote: If the terminal displays Ping Fails, check your network configurations.
entries.note: The page says it applies to Z1, Z8, Z9, Z11 and the QD models.

entries.title: Connect a touch-screen model to Ethernet
steps: The device can be on or off.
Connect the provided base port to the terminal.
Connect the Ethernet cable to the base port.
Connect the other end to your router or wired Ethernet outlet.
entries.quote: To connect to the ethernet, the device can be on or off
entries.note: Stax says the page covers the Z1, Z8, Z9, Z11, QD1, QD2, QD3, QD4 and QD5; the base-port steps are worded for the QD terminal.

entries.title: Check the Wi-Fi connection with a ping (touch screen)
steps: Tap the Wi-Fi symbol on the terminal.
Tap Ping.
Press 2 to ping Google.
The terminal shows whether the ping succeeded or failed. A successful ping shows an IP address.
entries.quote: If the ping was successful, you should see an IP address.

entries.title: Check the connection with a ping (non-touch Z8)
steps: Press F1.
Press F3.
Press 2 to ping Google.
entries.quote: For Non-Touchscreen models:

entries.title: Connect a Dejavoo PIN pad to the terminal by USB
steps: Unplug the power from the terminal before connecting the PIN pad.
Connect the straight USB end to the PIN pad.
Connect the L-shaped end to USB port 1 on the terminal (upside down, cord over the top).
Plug the power back into the terminal.
The terminal shows "Press OK when PIN Pad displays Welcome". Wait for the PIN pad to show Welcome, then press OK on the terminal.
The PIN pad loads its parameters automatically. Setup is complete when both devices show their ready screens.
entries.quote: Important: Unplug the power from your Dejavoo Terminal before connecting the PIN pad.
entries.note: Stax files this under Z Series Terminals and does not name the PIN pad model.

entries.title: Run the first sale through a connected PIN pad
steps: Enter the amount on the terminal's Credit Sale screen.
The terminal shows "waiting on PIN Pad".
The PIN pad shows "Tap, Insert, Swipe, and Enter Amount".
Process the card on the PIN pad.
The receipt prints when the sale succeeds.
entries.quote: Terminal shows "waiting on PIN Pad"
entries.note: Stax files this under Z Series Terminals and does not name the PIN pad model.

entries.title: Connecting a QD5 PIN pad to a QD4 terminal
steps: Stax publishes this as a video only: it shows how to connect a QD4 terminal to a QD5 PIN pad. No written steps are given on the page.
entries.quote: This video will show you how to connect your QD4 terminal to a QD5 pin pad.

entries.title: Run a debit sale on a Z-series terminal
steps: On the main screen, press the down arrow until debit is selected.
Press OK. The screen now says Debit Sale.
Enter the amount and press the green OK button.
Swipe the card and have the customer enter the PIN.
A receipt prints after the transaction is processed.
entries.quote: Click Ok to confirm. The screen will now say Debit Sale.

entries.title: Edit tip amounts by transaction number
steps: From the main screen press F3 for the favourites menu, or tap the star symbol on touch-screen models.
Select Edit All Trans# and press the green key.
Enter the transaction number from the original printed receipt.
Enter the tip amount. The base amount is shown too.
Press Yes with the green key to confirm.
Press the red X until you are back at the main screen, or go on to the next transaction number.
entries.quote: Use the keypad to enter the transaction number from the original printed receipt.

entries.title: Batched out without entering the tips
steps: Tips must be added by hand before you batch out for the day.
Tips cannot be adjusted after the batch has closed.
Contact your processor's support so the tip amounts can still be collected; Stax describes re-keying the sales from scanned receipts or creating a new sale for the tips.
entries.quote: If your business accepts tips, you must manually add them before you batch out for the day.
entries.note: The recovery process and phone numbers on the page are Stax's own.

entries.title: Turn the keyboard beep on or off
steps: From the main screen, press F1.
Scroll down and select Utility.
Enter the manager password (default 1234) and press the green OK key.
Select Settings and scroll down to Keyboard.
Press F1 to turn the beep on, or F3 to turn it off.
Press the red X to return to the main screen.
entries.quote: If you would like to turn on the beep, press F1. If you would like to turn it off, press F3.

entries.title: Reprint a receipt on a Z8
steps: Press the F3 button.
Use the arrow keys to select Reprint CR/DR Receipts.
Enter the password (1234 by default).
Choose the receipt: Last, by Transaction # or Card Number, and press OK.
Choose Merchant or Customer copy and press OK.
entries.quote: Select the receipt to reprint; Last, by Transaction #, or Card Number. Click Ok.

entries.title: Reset the Favorites menu to default on a Z8
steps: From the main screen, press F1 for the Service menu.
Select Core, then Utility, then Favorites.
Select Reset.
When asked Reset to Default, choose Yes.

entries.title: Technician steps: reinstall a corrupted DvPay / Aura app

Go back, press the 3 lines at the top right and find Apps.
Uninstall DVPAY/AURA. Open Market, Force Stop it, then go into Storage and Clear Data.
Open Market again and press the checkmark at the top right. Let Market finish updating, then install DvPay once Market says open.
Install the TPN: 3 lines at the bottom left, Utility, password 1234, Software Download, Connect, Network, Full, add the TPN and press the green button.

entries.title: Technician steps: factory reset a QD (Android) terminal
